title: Why Niger Can Seize Uranium but Cannot Sell It
date_evidence: April 24, 2026 (byline: Raphael Parens and Steven Radil)
key_claim: Niger's junta seized the Somair mine but cannot monetise the uranium, because selling it depends on ports, shipping control, insurance and verification systems it does not control; more than 1,000 metric tons of yellowcake sit at Airbase 101.
frame_summary: FPRI argues that weak states can now seize territorial assets more easily than before, but leverage in a fracturing international order sits in networked chokepoints, so seizure does not deliver revenue.
